findings.detail: The medium and long repeat the title, first sentence, date, agency and seventeen-member count nearly verbatim. The long then reproduces the supplied excerpt placeholder and generic “This entry is cataloged” rationale without adding further context.
The long contains an ellipsis excerpt marker plus the generic template claim that the account separates facts from broader conclusions. These are source-packet artifacts, not reader-facing writing.

The long says the attendance dispute “undercut” the administration’s claim of mass enthusiasm and characterizes the parade as a political celebration beyond an Army anniversary. Those conclusions go beyond the supplied figures and expert estimate.
The long repeats the medium’s date, parade, competing attendance figures and “No Kings” context. Most added text restates that the crowd dispute became part of the political story.

The long states that the category is retained and the assessment is preliminary pending further reporting. It also repeatedly inventories unknown orders, forests, legal procedures and implementation. These editing/source-audit notes interrupt the description of the announcement.

The long speculates about hiring criteria, Wise’s possible influence, and public confidence, then frames the event as an “insurrectionary episode” without describing the position or duties. Those broad implications are not grounded in the limited hiring facts supplied and displace the concrete event.

The long repeats the medium’s core account—the reported aid pause, officials surprised, Trump’s defensive-weapons remark, and his “I don’t know” response—almost line by line. It adds no substantial context beyond reiterating that the pause concerned one shipment.

The long quotes the supplied Truth Social excerpt but ends the quotation mid-sentence at “and” and then continues with an unrelated explanation. The source excerpt’s truncation has been carried into the reader-facing description.

The long repeatedly lists missing legal analysis, agency response, later outcome and additional information needed. The threat and the absence of an official step can be described without this extended source-audit close.

The long repeats the medium’s unnamed-source report, mixed verdict, lack of announcement and distinction between consideration and a granted pardon. It adds no substantial event context beyond restating these caveats.
The last two sentences repeat that the report described a possibility rather than a decision or completed pardon.
